re_apply_2026_08_06.commit_implies_assertions_passed: The migration is a single BEGIN…COMMIT. Its preconditions abort if bills_status_check is absent, if it already permits APPROVED, if any bill row falls outside the widened set, if customers lacks any column the mapping targets, or if customers.billing_address already exists. Its post-assertions abort if the widened constraint or either new column is missing, if the function body still names billing_address or internal_notes as identifiers, if the address is no longer decomposed onto address_line_1, if the cross-tenant entity check or the entity_type validation is missing, or if more than one create_customer_safe signature survives. The constraint and both columns are live, so the transaction committed, so every one of those held at commit time. That chain — not a ledger row — is what the structural results below rest on.

summary: DEF-026 + DEF-027. Widens bills_status_check to admit the APPROVED state that approve_bill_safe has written since December 2025, and repairs create_customer_safe, which inserted four columns that do not exist on public.customers. Replaces one CHECK constraint, adds two columns, re-issues one function body. No data is modified and no policy, trigger or index is touched.

def_026.defect: DEF-026, severity critical. Bill approval is broken on LIVE.
def_026.mechanism: approve_bill_safe sets status = 'APPROVED'. bills_status_check permits only ('DRAFT','AWAITING_PAYMENT','PART_PAID','PAID','OVERDUE','VOIDED'), so every approval raises 23514.
def_026.age: Since 20251217171128. That migration states its own intent in terms: 'Approve bill: No p_user_id, use auth.uid(), set status to APPROVED (not AWAITING_PAYMENT)'. The function was changed and the constraint was not — a half-applied design change, not a typo.
def_026.corroboration: The rest of the system already assumes APPROVED exists. record_bill_payment_safe accepts status IN ('APPROVED','AWAITING_PAYMENT','PART_PAID') in both 20251217224432 and the current 20260731210000 body, and 20251217171128 records reverse_bill_payment moving a bill AWAITING_PAYMENT -> APPROVED. Making approve_bill_safe write AWAITING_PAYMENT instead would strand those branches as dead code.
def_026.live_confirmation_2026_08_05: catalog_functions: approve_bill_safe (definition hash b4a2945c) writes 'APPROVED'. The constraint definition in git at 20260703145810 and 20260703195953 permits six values, none of them APPROVED.

def_027.defect: DEF-027, severity critical. Customer creation via the safe RPC is broken on LIVE.
def_027.mechanism: create_customer_safe inserts billing_address, company_name, default_currency and internal_notes. public.customers (20251205112122) has none of those columns, so every call raises 42703.
def_027.live_confirmation_2026_08_05: catalog_functions: create_customer_safe (definition hash ad24db0f) inserts all four. The table definition in git carries address_line_1/address_line_2/city/postcode/country and notes instead.

design_decisions.decision: DEF-026: widen the constraint rather than change what approve_bill_safe writes.
design_decisions.rationale: The APPROVED state was introduced deliberately and the payment and reversal paths already handle it. Making the function write AWAITING_PAYMENT would leave record_bill_payment_safe's APPROVED branch unreachable and contradict the documented reversal transition. Widening completes the change that was half-applied.

It is the pre-December name for the same approved-unpaid state, existing rows may still hold it, and every payment path treats the two as equivalent. Removing it would be an unannounced data migration with no evidenced need.

design_decisions.decision: DEF-026: no accounting impact, verified rather than assumed.
design_decisions.rationale: sync_bill_aged_balance drives amount_paid and remaining_balance from bill_payments and credit_note_allocations regardless of status, and its status transition excludes only ('voided','void','draft','cancelled'). An APPROVED bill is therefore aged, and transitions to PART_PAID/PAID, exactly as an AWAITING_PAYMENT one does. The change adds a state; it moves no figure.

design_decisions.decision: DEF-027: map billing_address onto the existing address columns instead of adding a jsonb column.
design_decisions.rationale: The caller (src/lib/customer-safe-service.ts) sends {line1, line2, city, postcode, country} — precisely the shape of the columns the table already has. Adding a jsonb billing_address beside them would give one customer's address two roots. A customer address feeds invoice projections, and under the filing-engine architecture a projection cannot have two sources of truth.

design_decisions.decision: DEF-027: map internal_notes onto the existing notes column.
design_decisions.rationale: Same concept under a different name. Adding a second free-text notes column would split the same information across two fields with no rule for which wins.

design_decisions.decision: DEF-027: add company_name and default_currency as real columns.
design_decisions.rationale: Unlike the other two these have no existing home and are genuine concepts. company_name is the legal or trading entity being invoiced, which is not the contact name in `name`. default_currency is the per-customer default that populates an invoice's currency. default_currency is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP' so existing rows are valid immediately and no backfill is required.

design_decisions.decision: DEF-027: validate p_entity_type, which the original never did.
design_decisions.rationale: customers_entity_check requires exactly one of client_id/company_id to be NOT NULL, and the body derives both from p_entity_type. Any value other than 'client' or 'company' left both NULL and surfaced as an opaque constraint violation. It now raises 22023 naming the field, matching create_invoice_draft_safe.

The body checked that the CALLER belongs to p_organization_id but never that p_entity_id does. A member of one organization could therefore attach a customer to another organization's client or company. create_invoice_draft_safe already carries this relationship check; create_customer_safe now carries the same one. This is a tenancy boundary repair found while fixing the column mismatch, and is called out here because it changes behaviour beyond the reported defect.

design_decisions.decision: Register bills.status in the CHECK-constraint drift registry.
design_decisions.rationale: bills was not in CHECK_CONSTRAINT_REGISTRY, which is exactly why an eight-month divergence between the function and the constraint went unseen. The registry drives both the unit test and the live smoke check, so adding it means any future divergence fails CI and the live probe. This is the systemic half of the fix; the constraint widening alone would leave the blind spot in place.

expected_objects.object: customers.company_name and customers.default_currency exist, default_currency NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP'

expected_objects.nullability_evidence: The 2026-08-06 capture selected column_name, data_type and column_default only — is_nullable was NOT read, so NOT NULL is not evidenced by catalog observation. It is evidenced by the DDL plus the commit: the migration issues ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS default_currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP', the column did not exist beforehand (the 2026-08-05 post-rollback capture returned 0 rows for it, so IF NOT EXISTS could not have skipped it), and the transaction committed. Stated so the weaker link is visible; a direct is_nullable read would settle it outright.

expected_objects.object: create_customer_safe inserts only columns that exist and returns success
expected_objects.verify_via: Reproduce first: call create_customer_safe pre-apply and confirm 42703. Post-apply, call it in a rolled-back transaction with a billing address and confirm the address lands decomposed across address_line_1/city/postcode/country.
expected_objects.actual: STRUCTURAL HALF PASSES. The migration's post-assertions read pg_proc.prosrc and abort unless the body names neither billing_address nor internal_notes as an identifier and does decompose onto address_line_1. It committed, so both held. The four non-existent columns are therefore gone from the INSERT, which is the 42703 cause.
expected_objects.why_still_partial: BEHAVIOURAL HALF UNVERIFIED. No invocation of create_customer_safe — pre-apply reproduction or post-apply call — is recorded anywhere in this repository. That the body no longer names a missing column is strong evidence it will not raise 42703; it is not the same as having called it and seen success:true with the address landing decomposed.

expected_objects.object: No billing_address column was added to public.customers
expected_objects.actual: Two independent grounds. (1) The migration's DEF-027 precondition RAISEs if customers.billing_address exists, and it committed, so the column was absent immediately before the ALTER. (2) The only ALTER TABLE public.customers in the file adds exactly company_name and default_currency. No statement in the file creates billing_address.

expected_objects.object: create_customer_safe refuses an entity belonging to another organization
expected_objects.verify_via: Call it as a member of org A passing a client id owned by org B — assert 42501 'Entity does not belong to organization'. Pre-apply this call SUCCEEDS, which is the point.
expected_objects.actual: STRUCTURAL: the migration's post-assertion aborts unless prosrc contains 'Entity does not belong to organization', and it committed, so the check is present in the live body.
expected_objects.why_still_partial: BEHAVIOURAL AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFERRED. The check being present in the body is not proof that the cross-tenant call is refused; only the call is. This is the one behaviour change that goes beyond the reported defect and the apply instructions require it to be seen to work. It has not been. Note additionally that the executor's route into this database is sandbox_exec, whose RLS bypass recurs (DEF-031), so a cross-tenant result obtained through that session would prove the in-function RAISE and not RLS — the DEF-031 receipt's evidence_rules govern how such a result may be recorded.

live_apply_attempt.diagnosis: The failing assertion is §6's `IF v_src LIKE '%billing_address,%' OR v_src LIKE '%internal_notes%'`. It reads pg_proc.prosrc, which is the BODY only — but the body legitimately references the PARAMETER p_internal_notes in the INSERT ... VALUES list. '%internal_notes%' therefore matches 'p_internal_notes' and the assertion fires against a body that is in fact correct. This is a false positive in the assertion, not a defect in the repair: the INSERT column list names only columns that exist. The same trap does not catch billing_address because that test is anchored with a trailing comma.
live_apply_attempt.not_edited: The file was NOT modified. Owner instruction: send the error rather than editing. A one-character-class fix (anchoring the internal_notes test the same way as billing_address, or testing the INSERT column list rather than the whole body) belongs on the PR branch and must come back through review.
